summary: Extract ANSWER line with choice-letter cleanup + stronger system prompt for format discipline

edits.hypothesis: Extracting the ANSWER: line and stripping appended descriptive text from choice-letter answers (e.g., '(D) Rodrigo' → '(D)') will fix format-mismatch failures without breaking clean outputs, since it's a safe cleanup only when format matches.
edits.targets_mode: answer extraction where model appends descriptions to choice letters ('(D) Rodrigo' vs '(D)', '(B) orange ball' vs '(B')
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Prompt-only instructions failed (E1-E3); code plumbing for safe extraction avoids redrawing R1's risky tool approach by keeping extraction simple and local.
edits.trigger_condition: When ANSWER: line exists and contains (LETTER) followed by extra text (detected as length>3 after closing paren)
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) The two shuffled_objects tasks with '(X) name' extraction errors would return clean (X) and match expected; (preservative) clean (A)–only answers pass through unchanged; multi-token answers like 'yes, no, no' have no parens so bypass the cleanup; (transfer) any task outputting choice letters with appended text benefits, generalizes beyond shuffled_objects
edits.regression_risk: If model outputs unexpected formats like nested parens or parens mid-string, the indexing could misfire; guarded by length and position checks to catch only the (LETTER) pattern.
edits.mechanism: Extracting the ANSWER: line and stripping appended descriptive text from choice-letter answers (e.g., '(D) Rodrigo' → '(D)') will fix format-mismatch failures without breaking clean outputs, since it's a safe cleanup only when format matches.

edits.hypothesis: Explicit system-level instruction emphasizing step-by-step reasoning AND strict answer format (single token, no extras) will reinforce discipline on both reasoning accuracy and format compliance, complementing the code cleanup with cognitive structure.
edits.targets_mode: reasoning errors where model rushes through logic, and format errors where model adds description
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Prior prompts (E1-E3) lacked specificity on execution discipline; this version separates formatting requirement (prose-level habit) from reasoning method (procedural), targeting both halves of the failure.
edits.trigger_condition: Always active; system prompt applied to every call.
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) Tasks failing on logic (wrong choice selected, wrong count) benefit from forced deliberation; tasks with format issues benefit from format reminder; (preservative) passing tasks (boolean_expressions-148, causal_understanding-025/023/136, linguini-188, object_properties-153, web_of_lies-074) see same system behavior, no regression expected; (transfer) step-by-step reasoning + format discipline is universal, generalizes to any logic/answer task
edits.regression_risk: If model becomes verbose and the code extraction catches only the first line, structured reasoning might output multi-line answers that get truncated; mitigated by testing on current successes (which already handle this format).
edits.mechanism: Explicit system-level instruction emphasizing step-by-step reasoning AND strict answer format (single token, no extras) will reinforce discipline on both reasoning accuracy and format compliance, complementing the code cleanup with cognitive structure.
